analysis: All units in this batch are documentation-only: unchanged historical CHANGELOG.md text (head lines 2128-2864) and removal of eight changelog.d/*.md fragments (desktop app, control API, hardware load, onboarding, signed preview, UI fixes, console desktop sign-in purpose, GLM OpenRouter returned-reasoning). No executable code, config, or protocol behavior changes in the supplied units. I checked these against the threat model (TB-002 WebSocket, TB-003 operator vs process, TB-007 inference engine, TB-011 App Attest, T-041 prefix cache) and found no regression, new attack surface, or invalidated assumption from these units. The fragment removals most likely reflect the fold-in of their content into the CHANGELOG.md v0.10.1 candidate section (head lines 11-138), which is outside the supplied units; I could not verify that the fragment text was actually carried over, but that is a documentation completeness matter, not a security regression. The CHANGELOG patch excerpt (truncated) describes a v0.10.1 candidate with a rollout dependency on coordinator darkbloom-platform#411 (refusing logprobs on GLM/MiMo/Nemotron before reservation) and an mlx-swift-lm pin bump (7bed8216 to 6148b6da, Swift-only). Those are described claims in prose; the actual code changes (GLM strict tools, reasoning handling, page-cache accounting for load admission, desktop control API loopback authentication, desktop login separate read-only session) live in other batches and need review there: notably the loopback control API authentication (TB-003), page-cache accounting affecting memory admission (T-016/TB-007 availability), and the cross-version coordinator dependency (TB-002 availability). No findings here.
